newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas rebounds on cold forecast, futures.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas rebounds on cold forecast, futures.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices for December recovered by about 20 cents Wednesday, led higher by colder weather forecasts for nearly the entire eastern half of the U.S. by the early part of next week and a rebound in the futures market.
Next-day prices in the Gulf climbed into the $3.60s to about $3.70, up at least 20 cents from Tuesday's levels but still about 10 cents under December indices.
In continuance of Tuesday's rally, NYMEX's January Henry Hub contract rose to a session high of $3.57 Wednesday, gaining another 20.6 cents.

The strength in the Gulf filtered into the Northeast markets as prices at the New York city-gate firmed by about 10 cents to the $4.20-4.50 range, but still lagged behind indices by more than 50 cents.
The coldest temperatures are anticipated in the lower northeastern states early next week, the National Weather Service reported.

The cold is also expected to land in the eastern midwestern states. As a result, prices on the Midcontinent pipes gained about 20 cents to the mid-$3.50s to low-$3.60s, converging with most December indices.
At the Chicago city-gate, prices were quoted in the anywhere from $3.68 to $3.78.
In west Texas, Permian gas prices jumped into the high-$3.50s, up about 10 cents from Tuesday, as the western third of the U.S. anticipated above- to much-above-normal temperatures by this weekend.
At the southern California border, prices were similarly higher in the low-$3.80s. Contributing to the strength were higher prices out of Canada due to stormy weather in the Northwest.
